sampling_model.design: Each site receives a known positive innovation-variance schedule normalized coordinatewise to the reference environment, \(d_{0j}=1\), and releases only coordinate ranks or a Kendall matrix. Absolute innovation multipliers, when experimentally recorded, are merely one interpretation whose reference ratios produce \(d\); they are not maintained inputs.
sampling_model.units: Within environment \(e\), \(n_e\) observations are independent and identically distributed from one continuous-margin Gaussian copula, and samples are independent across environments.
sampling_model.treatment: Environment \(e\) changes reference innovation variance \(v_j\) to \(v_jd_{ej}\) while leaving the structural matrix invariant.
sampling_model.overlap: Population identification requires a distinct normalized profile for every vertex pair; uniform inference also requires \(m\le d_{ej}\le M\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(R_e\) by the sine transform of the Kendall matrix; no marginal transformations, marginal variances, absolute excitation scales, or raw observations are pooled.

body.tldr: Known reference-normalized innovation multipliers can identify an invariant linear-Gaussian DAG even when every site releases only a Gaussian copula. The true structural coefficients are represented by the unit-free canonical matrix \(B^0=B^{\pi_0}(R_0)=H_0BH_0^{-1}\). Pairwise projective separation is the sharp universal generic frontier: wrong orders fail polynomial prediction identities, whereas tied profiles admit explicit reverse-edge and fork--chain twins. Exact all-order recovery uses signed squared-cross-product checks inside its construction, while the substantive conditional-pair theorem proves complete-DAG generic completeness and \(O(Ep^3)\) complexity. Uniform predictor bounds turn Kendall summaries into honest graph confidence sets under an explicit bounded normalized-excitation design regularity; the beta-min threshold, separation margin, and fallback are all expressed in reference-standardized units. Exact-once sparse-fiber enumeration remains open.

project_justification.gap: Montagna2025InvariancePrinciple, Section 3, Theorem 1, is the closest multiple-environment identifiability comparator, but it uses full environment densities through score and Hessian information and needs two auxiliary environments. BACKSHIFT uses covariance differences on a common numerical scale. GnIES arXiv:2211.14897v4, Theorem 6, uses full Gaussian environment distributions; the separate Journal of Machine Learning Research article by Taeb, Gamella, Heinze-Deml, and Bühlmann treats latent variables and unknown additive interventions. Invariant prediction tests stability of a response conditional law across environments, and conditional-variance identification uses scale-bearing observational quantities. None characterizes the full DAG fiber or honest support uncertainty from independently standardized correlations and a known normalized excitation schedule, including the reference-plus-one-environment frontier.
project_justification.niche: Acyclicity lets the reference correlation select one canonical standardized recursive model per order. The remaining correlations become predictions indexed only by the normalized schedule, so both identification and inference live on a diagonal-gauge quotient.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the universal generic if-and-only-if frontier and tied-profile necessity family, uses the reference-standardized coordinate \(B^0=H_0BH_0^{-1}\), gives a non-tautological conditional-pair completeness and cubic-complexity theorem for generic complete DAGs, and closes rank-summary inference under explicit gauge-invariant margins and bounded calibrated design profiles. Signed polynomial checks remain part of the exhaustive algorithm specification, not a separate contribution.

body.related_work: Montagna2025InvariancePrinciple, Section 3, Theorem 1, is the closest multiple-environment pairwise-noise-ratio identifiability comparator. It observes full environment densities and extracts score and Hessian information, using two auxiliary environments to form two Hessian-difference groups whose diagonal ratio has distinct entries. The present observation regime releases only independently standardized correlation orbits with known normalized excitation profiles and proves a sharp reference-plus-one-environment frontier; Montagna's density-level theorem therefore informs but does not subsume the projective-copula result. RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Section 2.4, equation (10), Theorem 1, and Appendix A, is a related identification template but starts from covariance differences measured on one common scale. For any positive diagonal \(H_e\), \(\operatorname{corr}(H_e\Sigma_eH_e)=R_e\), while changing one diagonal entry of one \(H_e\) changes a covariance difference; therefore independently standardized correlations do not determine BACKSHIFT's input. This is an elementary observation about the observation regime, not a theorem contribution. PetersBuhlmann2014EqualVariance, Theorem 1, supplies a recursive triangular-factorization precedent. PetersEtAl2016InvariantPrediction, Sections 2--3, intersects predictor sets whose conditional response law remains invariant across environments and provides confidence statements for causal predictors. That intervention-invariance observation is different from observing only standardized joint correlations: the present target is the whole DAG, and its identifying variation is a known coordinatewise normalized noise-variance schedule rather than an invariant response regression. GamellaEtAl2022GnIES is the GnIES manuscript arXiv:2211.14897v4: equations (1)--(5) specify independent Gaussian innovations with environment-varying diagonal noise covariance, and Theorem 6 states that, under its assumptions, the intervention-equivalence class equals the sparsest distribution-equivalent graphs. Its full Gaussian environment distributions reveal scale-bearing variance interventions; independently standardized correlations retain only the calibrated ratios \(d\), so the canonical projective predictor is not a GnIES score specialization. TaebEtAl2024Latent is the distinct Journal of Machine Learning Research 25(293) article about latent-variable models with unknown additive interventions. Park2020ConditionalVariance, Theorem 2, uses marginal and conditional variances from a full observational law, while YinEtAl2024HNM, equation (5) and Theorem 2, uses parent-dependent conditional-variance functions in a nonlinear heteroscedastic-noise model. Those conditional-variance observation models are not available after unrelated site standardization; the present model instead uses cross-environment correlation predictions and known normalized excitation profiles. LiuEtAl2012NPNskeptic, Theorem 4.2, supplies the uniform sine-transformed Kendall correlation bound, whereas Theorem 4.3 is only its plug-in transfer to undirected precision procedures. The fixed directed-support margin here is declared directly on \(B^0\), not attributed to either theorem or to VanDeGeerBuhlmann2013DAG's different rate-dependent all-order condition; the latter is only support-recovery precedent. MitraZhang2014RankCorrelation informs simultaneous matrix control. WangKolarDrton2025ConfidenceOrderings and StriederEtAl2021ConfidenceCausalDiscovery motivate preserving causal-order uncertainty. LiEtAl2024FedCDH supplies the federated consumer but communicates covariance tensors richer than Kendall releases. Afsari2008JDSensitivity supplies broader motivation from diagonalizer conditioning and uniqueness moduli; it is not a source for the imposed bounds \(m\le d_{ej}\le M\). WangEtAl2023EquivalenceEnumeration and WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration motivate canonical augmentation for the open sparse quotient problem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Generic identification is relative to each exact-support stratum and does not classify its real exceptional locus. Pairwise projective separation alone gives no uniform inference rate: coverage also uses correlation conditioning, the imposed bounded normalized-excitation design, reference-standardized beta-min, and wrong-order score separation. The cubic guarantee applies only to generic complete DAGs and uses exact-real rather than bit complexity. Unknown normalized schedules, cycles, latent confounding, varying mechanisms, singular correlations, zero innovation variances, unknown vertex correspondence, and discrete margins are outside the maintained model.
body.honest_scope: The supporting canonical-order lemma, universal generic frontier, tied-profile family, conditional-pair completeness and operation count, predictor perturbation bound, and finite-sample confidence theorem are proof obligations. The positivity, signed squared-cross-product, and deduplication steps specify exhaustive exact-real recovery and are not counted as theorem contributions; direct enumeration uses \(p!\) orders and \(O(Ep!p^3)\) arithmetic operations, excluding coefficient bit growth. Diagonal invariance of correlation and nonrecovery of covariance differences are elementary explanatory facts, not numbered claims. The normalized schedule \(d\), not any absolute multiplier array, is the maintained design input. Bounded schedule entries are an application-facing design regularity imposed for uniform constants, not a published standard condition. Bounded schedule-calibration error would add a predictor perturbation term that is subtracted from the wrong-order score-separation budget; the reference-standardized coefficient threshold is unchanged, and the stated theorem treats exact calibration. The confidence theorem uses only the unit-free matrix \(B^0\) for coefficient separation and returns all labeled DAGs whenever the same normalized thresholds cannot certify inversion. As supporting evidence, for \(p=3\), \(B_{21}=B_{31}=B_{32}=1\), \(v=(1,1,1)\), and \(d_1=(1,4,9)\), the unreleased representatives \(\Sigma_0=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1&2\\1&2&3\\2&3&6\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\Sigma_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1&2\\1&5&6\\2&6&17\end{psmallmatrix}\) induce the released correlations \(R_0=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1/\sqrt2&\sqrt{2/3}\\1/\sqrt2&1&\sqrt3/2\\\sqrt{2/3}&\sqrt3/2&1\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(R_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1/\sqrt5&2/\sqrt{17}\\1/\sqrt5&1&6/\sqrt{85}\\2/\sqrt{17}&6/\sqrt{85}&1\end{psmallmatrix}\). Their first-pair shifted-odds comparisons are \(1/4,4/13,1/4,36/49,4/13,36/49\) against the six order predictions \(1/4,2/9,4,4/3,18,27/4\), excluding all five wrong orders exactly. This calculation is evidence, not a numbered claim. Two environments with pairwise distinct relative multipliers provide the required sanity reduction. Sparse output-sensitive exact-once enumeration is open.
